newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: High call rates keep Sri Lanka rupee buoyant.
newsitem.headline: High call rates keep Sri Lanka rupee buoyant.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee remained strong throughout the day on the back of high call money rates, as banks sold dollars for rupees, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 56.55 to the dollar after opening at 56.65, which was slightly lower than its previous closing level of 56.64.
"The dollar eased throughout because banks sold the currency to generate rupees," said a dealer at Standard Chartered Bank.
He said the dollar could even slip to 56.30-56.20 rupees this week, if money rates stay high.
Call money closed at 26 percent after rising to a high of 30, dealers said.

The central bank's withdrawal of one billion rupees at last week's treasury bill auctions, and panic borrowing by banks who expect interest rates to rise in the last quarter, was keeping call money rates high, they said.
"Last year's experience where rates averaged over 25 percent in the last quarter, is still fresh in the minds of dealers," said the Standard Chartered dealer.
